rationale: Round 1 compiled and passed, so this round raises aggressiveness across the board: SUB, BCF, and IBR get the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights since arithmetic substitution, bogus control flow, and indirect branching give strong static-analysis resistance at modest cost on this small (969-byte text) binary; SPLIT stays cheap and low-risk to help FLA/BCF divide the few basic blocks available in main and sieve; ICALL and IGV are pushed up to diversify call sites and global layout, which is especially valuable with only four functions where inter-function structure is trivially recoverable. RuntimeCost and SizeCost tolerances are raised moderately (0.30-0.55) to allow the pass selector to accept more overhead given the previous clean build, but FLA's RuntimeCost stays the highest at 0.55 because sieve's hot loops are runtime-sensitive and flattening adds a dispatch loop on every iteration; CorrectnessRisk weights remain low (0.05-0.20) to preserve the demonstrated correctness while still favoring passes like SPLIT and IBR that have the safest transformation profiles.
